name: repeat rounds of byte substitution, positional permutation and round-key mixing
mechanism: arrange the block as a small grid of bytes; each round replaces every byte through a fixed nonlinear table, moves bytes to new positions, mixes each column linearly, and XORs in a round key derived from the master key; a dozen rounds make every output bit depend nonlinearly on every input and key bit; decryption runs the inverse steps backward

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), winner of NIST competition, also known as Rijndael' in section Computer science / Cryptography:

requires: a substitution table and a key schedule (data)
fails_when: table lookups leak through cache timing without constant-time implementation
instances: Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), winner of NIST competition, also known as Rijndael
